findings.prerequisite: An attacker can write a cache directory that the application later reads using pickle deserialization.
findings.usage: Current OpenBB provider cache helpers, including ECB, CFTC, Federal Reserve, FRED, SEC, TMX and USDA.
mitigations: Separate trusted service, with no agent workspace mounted.
Private owned state root and cache/temp/data/export directories; managed directory symlinks rejected.
Fresh workers with umask 0077, private HOME/cache/temp paths and fixed installed modules.
No caller-controlled cache destination or cache restore endpoint.
findings.residual_risk: Filesystem isolation is required. Same-identity processes, host compromise or importing an untrusted cache can still enable malicious deserialization. No upstream patch is present.
operator_requirements: Keep cache state inaccessible to agent boxes and unrelated services.
Never import caches from untrusted origins; discard state if ownership is uncertain.
Set a filesystem or volume quota; per-request controls do not cap lifetime cache growth.
Recheck releases and advisory applicability during dependency updates.
